parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented facility exclusion, border friction, police targeting or trans-specific violence; foreign passports appear to be accepted and public pride events have run without official impediment. But the positives are thin and largely LGB-focused: the dossier shows no operating visitor-facing remedy (no enforced service-equality regime, no demonstrated prosecution/compensation for anti-trans refusal), a dead-letter sodomy statute whose 2024 decriminalisation is still under government appeal, and documented administrative defiance of court rulings on LGBT matters — a rule-of-law weakness that discounts paper protections. Organised political hostility exists (anti-gay party, governing-party youth league), though no confrontation or violence against travellers is recorded. Resident-only gaps — case-by-case gender-marker orders, no enumerated equality protection, psychologist regulations framing gender identity as disorder — are climate signals, not traveller exposure. This sits at the acceptance-without-enforceable-protection tier, below 0.65–0.75 anchors that document remedies actually working.
